observations: Main ridge, canopy peak, doorway threshold and stair foot are close to the reference composition at a 1.35 m eye height.
The dark blue grey ceramic roof and layered karahafu recess improve on the baseline, but the entrance still reads as an evenly lit framework.
Foreground slabs are visibly convex, pale blue grey, and separated by excessive black gaps.
Stair treads show an unnatural repeated high contrast grid.
Gallery retaining walls are broad undecorated pale planes; the garden does not transition naturally to the raised building floor.
Overhead maple leaves look like pale paper clusters and the pine foliage remains visually sparse.
secondPassChanges: Construct continuous sloped earth embankments, embedded rocks and rooted three dimensional shrubs around the stairs.
Add individually jointed chipped retaining stones to exposed platform faces.
Reduce slab relief to millimetres, reduce joints to centimetres, use dark warm stone albedo and local wet roughness rather than a bright uniform clear coat.
Reduce stair surface relief and bump scale to remove the repeated glints.
Use deep warm brown red timber materials, lower environment fill and a more lateral physical sun angle for deeper self shadowing.
Curl the maple leaf geometry along raised central veins, use darker leaf and bark materials, and increase the layered plant volume.
